original:
@advc:  pagestep sp, @runnext
        jmp @runnext
proposal:
@advc:
  .if BHW
        pagestep sp, @runnext
        jmp @runnext
  .else
        clc                         ; C = 0 for @runnext (the bcs's 1)
        inc sp+1                    ; N set: ran off the end
        bpl @runnext
        lda #>RINGBASE
        sta sp+1
:       jmp @runnext                ; (':' keeps pagestep's anonymous label count)
        .assert <RINGBYTES = 0 && RINGEND = $8000, error, "@advc: the Master's ring"
  .endif
assumption: The Master's pagestep (macros.s 186-193) is: inc p+1 / bpl : / lda #>RINGBASE / sta p+1 / : clc. It emits one anonymous label. @runnext needs C = 0 (comment at line 434; @run needs C = 0 per drawrect's invariants) and reads no other flag. @runnext is about 50 bytes back, so it is in bpl's reach. The anonymous references from line 380 on (490/492/496/508, in @mir, local) all fall after this range and keep their targets because the count is kept.
anon_change: none: the Master still emits exactly one ':' here (it moves from before the clc to the jmp, and nothing branches to it); the Model B is unchanged (pagestep with a back target emits none)
argument: Master, common path (no ring end): before, inc sp+1 (5) + bpl taken (3) + clc (2) + jmp (3) = 13; after, clc (2) + inc sp+1 (5) + bpl @runnext taken (3) = 10. sp+1 gets the same value, C = 0, and A is untouched, as before. Fold path: before, inc / bpl not taken / lda #>RINGBASE / sta sp+1 / clc / jmp; after, clc / inc / bpl not taken / lda / sta / jmp, which gives the same sp+1, A, and C = 0, at the same 17 cycles. The saving is 3 cy x 6.3 executions a frame, or 2 cy if the backward bpl crosses a page (the applier's pads decide). Model B: the same tokens as before.

original:
@rfold: ringfold rc_sp
        sta rc_sp+1
        sta sp+1
        lda rc_sp                   ; (the Model B's fold moves the low byte too)
        sta sp
        rts
proposal:
@rfold: ringfold rc_sp
        sta rc_sp+1
        sta sp+1
  .if BHW
        lda rc_sp                   ; (the Model B's fold moves the low byte too)
        sta sp
  .endif
        rts
assumption: The Master's ringfold (macros.s 113-115: sec / sbc #>RINGBYTES) does not touch rc_sp. Line 446 has already stored sp = rc_sp's low byte. After @drawrow's rts, A is dead. The callers at @rowy/@second go straight to dec rc_h / beq, then lda #32 / lda ptr / @done's rts, and on the normal @rowdone path drawrect already exits with A = the high byte. drawrect documents A as clobbered.
argument: On the Master, lda rc_sp / sta sp rewrites sp's low byte with the value it already holds (from line 446, and the Master's fold leaves rc_sp alone), so sp, rc_sp and C (from the sbc) come out the same. Only A at the rts changes, to the high byte, which is what the normal @rowdone path returns, and every consumer overwrites it first. N/Z are reset by the callers' dec rc_h. Saving: 6 cy x 0.8 executions a frame on the Master. The Model B assembles the same code.

original:
@runnext:                           ; C = 0 (the loop back's)
        lda #4
        sta rc_lim
        lda rc_sub
        sta rowoff
        inc rc_gi
        jmp @run
proposal:
@runnext:                           ; C = 0 (the loop back's)
        ldx rc_gi                   ; the row's first run? only it leaves rc_lim, rowoff
        bne @rnx                    ; to set (a later run's are 4 and rc_sub already)
        lda #4
        sta rc_lim
        lda rc_sub
        sta rowoff
@rnx:   inx
        stx rc_gi
        jmp @run+2                  ; past @run's ldx rc_gi (zp, 2 bytes): X = rc_gi
segment: TILCODE (bank 6 on the Model B; has room). Code after @runnext (@rowdone, @advc, @hfill/@solid, the PCHAR blocks, the dispatch tables) moves 5 bytes on: the >@f7 = >@f31 and RUN1/RUN8 page asserts and pads may need the applier's re-tune
assumption: rc_gi is zero page (engine/vars.s line 93, inside the .zeropage section opened at line 51), so @run's first instruction `ldx rc_gi` (tiles.s 314) is 2 bytes and @run+2 is `lda GATHERH,x`. rc_lim and rowoff are written only by @drawrow/its caller at a row's start (tiles.s 240-252, 303-305) and by @runnext; nothing between runs of one row writes them (grep: the only other readers are RUNN, @full, @hcopy, @mir). rc_gi is 0 at a row's first run (@drawrow line 302-303) and incremented only here, so rc_gi = 0 at @runnext exactly for the row's first run. X and A are dead at @runnext (the original's @run reloads X from rc_gi; A is reloaded by lda GATHERH,x). All entries to @runnext (fall-through from @advsp's bcs, the Model B pagestep's bcc, the Master's jmp at 463, @mir's jmp) only need C = 0 kept, and nothing here touches C.
argument: First run of a row (rc_gi = 0): the same stores as before (rc_lim = 4, rowoff = rc_sub), then rc_gi = 1 and X = 1 entering @run's lda GATHERH,x -- exactly what inc rc_gi / jmp @run / ldx rc_gi produced. Later runs (rc_gi >= 1): rc_lim is already 4 and rowoff already rc_sub (set by the first run's @runnext, untouched since), so skipping the stores leaves memory identical; rc_gi and X advance as before. C untouched on both paths (ldx/bne/lda/sta/inx/stx/jmp). Cycles: original 22 (incl. @run's ldx); first run 24 (+2), later runs 14 (-8, -7 if bne crosses a page). Rows with 2+ runs <= 23.3 (B) / 29.9 (M) a frame against 49.1 / 53.5 non-last runs: net >= ~25.8x8-23.3x2 = ~160 B, ~23.6x8-29.9x2 = ~129 M (more if many rows are single-run). Note this trades the first run's path (+2) for the later runs' (-8).

original:

proposal:
@advc:

  .else

        inc sp+1                    ; N set: ran off the end
        bpl @runnext

segment: TILCODE (Master only; Model B unchanged byte for byte)
assumption: pagestep's Master expansion (macros.s 186-193) is inc p+1 / bpl : / lda #>RINGBASE / sta p+1 / : clc. @runnext needs only C = 0 (A, X dead: it reloads both); @runnext is ~20-40 bytes above @advc, in bpl/bra reach. The Model B branch is the unchanged pagestep plus jmp.

argument: Master, no fold: original inc / bpl taken / clc / jmp = 5+3+2+3 = 13; new clc / inc / bpl taken = 2+5+3 = 10 (11 if bpl crosses a page): sp+1 and C = 0 identical, A untouched in both. Fold: original inc/bpl/lda/sta/clc/jmp = 17, new clc/inc/bpl/lda/sta/bra = 17: sp+1 = >RINGBASE, C = 0 in both (clc before inc: inc, lda, sta do not touch C). 3 cycles x ~6.3 entries a frame (line 463's Master count).

original:
lda #0
        sta rc_gi                   ; the run's index into GATHERL/H
proposal: stz rc_gi                   ; the run's index into GATHERL/H
assumption: cpu.inc: on the Model B the stz macro expands to exactly `lda #0 / sta rc_gi` (cpu.inc line 241-248), and on the Master it is the native stz. A is dead after it: the next instruction is `lda rc_sc0` (line 304), and Z from `lda #0` is overwritten by that load before anything reads it.
argument: Model B: the macro expands to the same two instructions, so the bytes and cycles are identical. Master: stz zp (3 cycles, 2 bytes) stores the same 0 as lda #0 / sta zp (5 cycles, 4 bytes). The only difference is that A is no longer 0 afterwards, and lda rc_sc0 overwrites A, N and Z at once. C is not touched on either form, and the clc comes later at line 308. Executions: 29.9 a frame on the Master.

original:
beq @done
@nextrow:
        ; ---- one map row on
        lda ptr
        clc
        adc MAPSTRIDE
        sta ptr
        lda ptr+1
        adc MAPSTRIDE+1
        sta ptr+1
        jmp @rowy
proposal:
beq @done
@nextrow:
        ; ---- one map row on
        lda ptr
        clc
        adc MAPSTRIDE
        sta ptr
        lda ptr+1
        adc MAPSTRIDE+1
        sta ptr+1
        ; ---- @rowy's again, in line: the loop closes on a bne to @second, not a jmp
        jsr mapstrip
        stz rc_sub                  ; the tile's top char row: offset 0
        lda rc_ro0
        sta rowoff
        lda #8
        sta rowbit
        jsr @drawrow
        dec rc_h
        bne @second                 ; (0: falls into @done)
assumption: The copy matches @rowy's body (lines 237-247) instruction for instruction. @rowy keeps its label and its other entry (the `beq @rowy` at line 230). @done follows at line 268, so a fall-through reaches it. bne @second is in reach: @second to the new bne is about 60 bytes. The stz macro (cpu.inc) emits no anonymous labels, and no named label is added, so the @ scope is unchanged. The code after this grows by about 19 bytes (B) or 17 (M); the PAD/SAMEPAGE placement of the hot stretches must be re-tuned by the applier.
argument: Old path for each tile row after the first: jmp @rowy (3), then @rowy's body, then dec rc_h / beq @done not taken (2), then @second. New path: the same body in line, then dec rc_h / bne @second taken (3, or 4 if it crosses a page). That saves 2 cycles, or 1 if it crosses. When rc_h reaches 0 after that row, the old path was jmp 3 plus beq taken 3, and the new one is bne not taken 2, which falls into @done: 4 saved. The registers, memory and flags at @second and @done are identical. In both versions the last instruction before @second is a dec rc_h with Z=0, and the one before @done is a dec rc_h with Z=1; the stores, calls and arguments are the same. Executions: 9.7 a frame (B), 12.8 (M).

original:
lda #0
        sta rc_gi                   ; the run's index into GATHERL/H
proposal: stz rc_gi                   ; the run's index into GATHERL/H
assumption: cpu.inc's stz macro on BHW=1 expands to exactly 'lda #0 / sta arg' (cpu.inc:241-248), so the Model B assembles the same bytes; on the Master it is native stz (cpu.inc:222 area). A is dead: the next instruction (line 304) is 'lda rc_sc0', and nothing between reads A or the Z/N flags from the lda #0. tiles.s already uses the stz macro in this routine (line 240, stz rc_sub).
argument: Model B: byte-identical expansion, no change. Master: stz rc_gi (3 cy zp) replaces lda #0 (2) + sta rc_gi (3); rc_gi gets the same 0; A is overwritten by lda rc_sc0 next, whose load also sets N/Z afresh; C untouched in both forms (clc follows at 308 anyway). 29.9 executions a frame x 2 cycles.

original:
and rowbit
        beq @hcopy
        jmp @hfill
        ; no: the stored row -- GATHERL's bits $E0, (k&7)<<5, with rowoff's others,
        ; this run's char offset less the row's 32 (the two eors merge them)
@hcopy: lda GATHERL,x
        eor rowoff
proposal:
bit rowbit                  ; (A kept: GATHERL,x for @hcopy)
        beq @hcopy
        jmp @hfill
        ; no: the stored row -- GATHERL's bits $E0, (k&7)<<5, with rowoff's others,
        ; this run's char offset less the row's 32 (the two eors merge them)
@hcopy: eor rowoff                  ; A = GATHERL,x still (the bit kept it)
assumption: rowbit is zero page (vars.s:200, segment ZPF5) so 'bit rowbit' is bit zp, 3 cycles/2 bytes, same as 'and rowbit'. @hcopy is reached only from line 280's beq (grep: no other reference). @hfill (line 538) begins with 'lda GATHERL,x', so it does not read A, and its path reads no V flag: there is no bvc/bvs/clv anywhere in tiles.s (grep). X = rc_gi unchanged across these lines.
argument: bit rowbit sets Z = (A & rowbit) == 0 exactly as 'and rowbit' did, so beq goes the same way, and C is untouched by both. Fill path (to @hfill): same cycles, A and N/V differ, but @hfill reloads A at once and nothing on that path reads N or V before they are rewritten. Copy path (@hcopy): A already holds GATHERL,x (bit does not change A), so the reload 'lda GATHERL,x' (4 cycles, +1 on a page cross) is dropped. The eor/and/eor that follow get the same input and give the same tp. Saves 4 cycles on each of about 7.0 (B) and 8.0 (Master) @hcopy runs a frame. No path is slower.

original:
ldy #8*c
        sta (sp),y
        lda tp+1
        iny
proposal:
.if c = 0 .and .not ::BHW
        sta (sp)                    ; line 0 non-indexed (Master)
        lda tp+1
        ldy #1
.else
        ldy #8*c
        sta (sp),y
        lda tp+1
        iny
.endif
assumption: sp is a zero-page pointer (already used as (sp),y). PCHAR is used only at lines 589-592 (grep); the Master reaches @f7 only via jmp (@ft-2,x) through .word addresses (no size-dependent offsets; the @fto/@f page asserts are .if BHW only). CHARCPY 0 already uses the same .if ::BHW / native lda (tp) pattern inside a macro, so the 65C02 (zp) form assembles in the Master build. PCHAR documents A, Y clobbered, C kept; X untouched.
argument: Model B: the .if is false, the original four lines assemble unchanged (identical bytes and cycles). Master, PCHAR 0 only: original ldy #0 (2) + sta (sp),y (6) + lda tp+1 (3) + iny (2) = 13 cycles leaves line 0 = tp, A = tp+1, Y = 1; new sta (sp) (5) stores A=tp to (sp)+0, lda tp+1 (3), ldy #1 (2) = 10 cycles leaves the same A and Y (and Y is reloaded by ldy #8*c+3 next anyway). Stores happen in the same order to the same addresses. Flags: sta sets none; lda tp+1 then ldy #1 vs lda tp+1 then iny: N/Z from Y=1 in both cases (N=0,Z=0); C untouched by all (needed by @advsp). 3 cycles saved per @f7 execution, ~30.4 a frame on the Master; 5 bytes -> 4.

original:
ldy #k
        lda L0TAB,x
        sta (sp),y
        iny
proposal:
.if (k = 0) .and (.not ::BHW)
        lda L0TAB,x                 ; line 0 non-indexed
        sta (sp)
        ldy #1
    .else
      .if (k <> 0) .or (.not ::BHW)
        ldy #k                      ; (Model B k = 0: Y = 0 from ldaz)
      .endif
        lda L0TAB,x
        sta (sp),y
        iny
    .endif
segment: SPR4CODE and SPR5CODE (each copy of NIB_LOOPS; sprFN_0 only, the k=0 pair of the unmirrored cells)
assumption: NPAIR is only instantiated by NIBCELLS (sprloops.s 217-225), so k=0 is always reached through the macro's own `ldaz ptr` (line 70). On the Model B ldaz expands to `ldy #0 / lda (ptr),y` (cpu.inc 294-297), so Y=0; lines 75-78 (beq, tax, lda NMASK,x, beq opq) do not touch Y, so Y=0 at opq. On the Master ldaz is `lda (ptr)` (cpu.inc 207) and Y is unknown, hence the Master form sets Y=1 itself before the indexed store. NPAIR's contract says Y is clobbered on exit; the code after it (the next NPAIR's ldy #k/2, or sprretP / jmp ret) does not read Y, and after the rewrite Y is 1 on both machines, as it was.
argument: Model B k=0: the same instructions minus `ldy #0`, which reloads the 0 that ldaz already put in Y: the same stores to (sp)+0 and (sp)+1, and Y=1 at the end. Saves 2 cycles per opaque k=0 pair. Master k=0: `sta (sp)` writes to the same address as `ldy #0 / sta (sp),y` (5 cycles against 2+6), and `ldy #1` gives the same Y and N/Z as `iny` from 0. Nothing reads the flags: the next instruction is `lda L1TAB,x`. Saves 3 cycles (24 -> 21). k>0 and the mirrored instances assemble exactly as before. About 24 executions a frame on the B and 27 on the Master (k=0 is ~23% of pairs: 308-237 on the B).

original:
sta sp_msk
        ldy #k
        lda (sp),y
        and sp_msk
  .if mirror
        ldy L0TAB,x                 ; the line's byte, straight into SWAPTAB's index
        ora SWAPTAB,y
        ldy #k                      ; Y back for the store
  .else
        ora L0TAB,x
  .endif
        sta (sp),y
        iny
proposal:
sta sp_msk
  .if (k = 0) .and (.not ::BHW)
        lda (sp)                    ; line 0 non-indexed
        and sp_msk
    .if mirror
        ldy L0TAB,x                 ; the line's byte, straight into SWAPTAB's index
        ora SWAPTAB,y
    .else
        ora L0TAB,x
    .endif
        sta (sp)
        ldy #1
  .else
    .if (k <> 0) .or mirror .or (.not ::BHW)
        ldy #k                      ; (Model B k = 0 unmirrored: Y = 0 from ldaz)
    .endif
        lda (sp),y
        and sp_msk
    .if mirror
        ldy L0TAB,x                 ; the line's byte, straight into SWAPTAB's index
        ora SWAPTAB,y
        ldy #k                      ; Y back for the store
    .else

    .endif
        sta (sp),y
        iny
  .endif
segment: SPR4CODE and SPR5CODE (each copy; sprFN_0 masked k=0 on both machines, and sprFM_0 masked on the Master)
assumption: As in the opaque candidate: k=0 is always reached through `ldaz ptr` (line 70). On the Model B that leaves Y=0 (cpu.inc 294-297), and in the unmirrored instance nothing between it and line 86 touches Y (beq, tax, lda NMASK,x, beq not taken). The mirrored instance does `tay` (line 82), so its ldy #0 stays on the B. On the Master Y is unknown at k=0, and the new form loads Y=1 before the next indexed access (line 98's `lda (sp),y`). sp_msk is written before it is read, as before. Lines 98-107 that follow need Y=1 and A free, and they get them.
argument: Master k=0: `lda (sp)` and `sta (sp)` touch (sp)+0 exactly as `ldy #0 / lda (sp),y` and `sta (sp),y` do. A is computed the same way (AND the mask, OR the line byte, straight or through SWAPTAB), and `ldy #1` replaces `iny` from 0, so the next line's `lda (sp),y` reads (sp)+1 as before. Nothing reads the flags: `lda (sp),y` comes next. Unmirrored: 22 -> 19 cycles. Mirrored: 28 -> 23 (both `ldy #0` gone, and `sta (zp)` costs 5 against 6). Model B k=0 unmirrored: only the redundant `ldy #0` goes (Y is already 0 from ldaz), so 2 cycles saved. The B's mirrored and k>0 instances assemble byte for byte as before. About 6 B and 7 M unmirrored, and 4 M mirrored, executions a frame.

original:
ldy L0TAB,x
        lda SWAPTAB,y
        ldy #k
        sta (sp),y
proposal:
ldy L0TAB,x
        lda SWAPTAB,y
    .if (k = 0) .and (.not ::BHW)
        sta (sp)                    ; line 0 non-indexed
    .else
        ldy #k
        sta (sp),y
    .endif
segment: SPR4CODE and SPR5CODE (Master: sprFM_0's opaque k=0 pair)
assumption: Master only (the B assembles exactly as now). After this store, the following lines 117-120 (`ldy L1TAB,x / lda SWAPTAB,y / ldy #k+1 / sta (sp),y`) reload Y before every use, so dropping `ldy #0` leaves no reader of the old Y=0. At the macro's end Y = k+1 = 1, unchanged.
argument: On the Master `sta (sp)` stores A to (sp)+0 as `ldy #0 / sta (sp),y` does, in 5 cycles against 8. The flags differ (ldy #0 set Z), but the next instruction is `ldy L1TAB,x`, which sets them again, and nothing in between reads them. Y is overwritten at line 117 before any use. About 15 executions a frame on the Master (k=0 share of 66.5). The Model B is unchanged.

original:
tay
        lda SWAPTAB,y               ; the mask, mirrored
proposal: eor #$FF                    ; the mask, mirrored: NMASK's masks are $CC/$33, swapped
segment: SPR4CODE and SPR5CODE (each NPAIR mirror instance: 4 in sprFM, so -8 bytes a bank)
assumption: On this path (byte b != 0, NMASK[b] != 0) NMASK[b] is $33 or $CC: verified build/modelb/nibtab.bin and build/master/nibtab.bin (identical) NMASK = bytes 512..767 take only {0,$33,$CC,$FF}, $FF only at b=0 which beq done has already removed. SWAPTAB (banks.s SWAP_TABLE: bits 7<->4, 6<->5, 3<->0, 2<->1) maps $CC->$33 and $33->$CC, which equals EOR $FF for exactly those two values. Y is dead after: the next Y use is ldy #k (line 86). No flags consumed (sta sp_msk next).
argument: For both values the masked path can see, SWAPTAB[m] = m EOR $FF, so A (and therefore sp_msk) is the same. Y differs (tay no longer sets it) but line 86 reloads Y before use. Was tay 2 + lda abs,y 4 = 6 cycles, now 2: 4 cycles on every mirrored masked pair. Relies on the game's nibtab keeping nibble-0-transparent masks ($CC/$33), which is structural to the 4-bit format.

original:
ldy #k
        lda L0TAB,x
        sta (sp),y
        iny
proposal:
.if k = 0 && .not ::BHW
        lda L0TAB,x
        sta (sp)                    ; line 0 non-indexed
        ldy #1
  .else
    .if k <> 0
        ldy #k
    .endif                          ; (Model B k 0: Y = 0 still, from ldaz)
        lda L0TAB,x
        sta (sp),y
        iny
  .endif
segment: SPR4CODE and SPR5CODE (one instance a bank: sprFN_0's pair)
assumption: cpu.inc: on the Model B ldaz ptr (line 70, k = 0) is ldy #0 / lda (ptr),y, so Y = 0; between it and opq only beq done, tax, lda NMASK,x, beq opq run (no Y write), and opq is reached only from line 78 (it is .local). On the Master (65C02 .setcpu) sta (zp) is 5 cycles vs ldy #0 2 + sta (zp),y 6. Line 127's sta (sp),y needs Y = 1, given by ldy #1 / iny.
argument: Model B k=0: Y is already 0, so ldy #0 is dropped; stores and Y=1 for line 127 identical; -2 cycles. Master k=0: sta (sp) writes the same address as sta (sp),y with Y=0, ldy #1 leaves Y as iny did (flags not consumed: line 126 lda resets N/Z); 10 cycles -> 7. k != 0 instances assemble exactly as before. Estimate ~23% of pairs are k=0 (237 of 308 run ldy #k/2), applied to the 103.6/117.7 opaque unmirrored executions.

ldy #k
        sta (sp),y
proposal:
.if k = 0 && .not ::BHW
        sta (sp)                    ; line 0 non-indexed
  .else
        ldy #k
        sta (sp),y
  .endif
segment: SPR4CODE and SPR5CODE (Master only: sprFM_0's pair)
assumption: Master is 65C02 (.setcpu in cpu.inc .if .not BHW). Lines 117-120 reload Y (ldy L1TAB,x, then ldy #k+1) before the next use, so Y's value after line 116 is dead.
argument: For k=0 on the Master, sta (sp) stores to the same address as ldy #0 / sta (sp),y; Y is overwritten at line 117 and no flags are consumed (lda SWAPTAB,y at 118 sets them). 8 cycles -> 5 per mirrored opaque k=0 pair (~15 a frame). Model B and k != 0 unchanged.

original:
sta sp_msk
        ldy #k
        lda (sp),y
        and sp_msk
  .if mirror
        ldy L0TAB,x                 ; the line's byte, straight into SWAPTAB's index
        ora SWAPTAB,y
        ldy #k                      ; Y back for the store
  .else
        ora L0TAB,x
  .endif
        sta (sp),y
        iny
        lda (sp),y
        and sp_msk
proposal:
.if mirror
        sta sp_msk
  .endif
  .if k = 0 && .not ::BHW
        lda (sp)                    ; line 0 non-indexed
  .else
    .if k <> 0 || mirror
        ldy #k
    .endif                          ; (Model B k 0 unmirrored: Y = 0 still, from ldaz)
        lda (sp),y
  .endif
  .if mirror
        and sp_msk
        ldy L0TAB,x                 ; the line's byte, straight into SWAPTAB's index
        ora SWAPTAB,y
    .if k = 0 && .not ::BHW
        sta (sp)
    .else
        ldy #k                      ; Y back for the store
        sta (sp),y
    .endif
  .else
        and NMASK,x                 ; the mask straight from its table
        ora L0TAB,x
    .if k = 0 && .not ::BHW
        sta (sp)
    .else
        sta (sp),y
    .endif
  .endif
  .if k = 0 && .not ::BHW
        ldy #1
  .else
        iny
  .endif
        lda (sp),y
  .if mirror
        and sp_msk
  .else
        and NMASK,x
